sources.title: Statement: Direct to Device licence exemption regulations update
sources.lines: official HTML summary and document list, updated 18 June 2026
facts: Ofcom made amending regulations for licence-exempt SIM-enabled devices connecting to D2D satellite services in specified 900 MHz frequencies.
The regulations were intended to enter into force on 10 July 2026.
The page separates the April consultation, June statement and earlier authorisation decisions.

sources.title: Statement: Proposals for revising and improving our NGSO licensing process
sources.lines: official HTML decision summary, updated 24 March 2026
facts: Ofcom revised the NGSO licensing process to clarify evidence requirements and reduce coordination and administrative burdens.
The decision no longer routinely consults on NGSO gateway applications while extending the commenting period for network applications.
Updated guidance and application forms were published in March 2026.

sources.title: Apply for a non-geostationary satellite earth station licence
facts: NGSO earth-station authorisations cover network user terminals and gateway earth stations.
Licences can support consumer, business, government and Internet of Things connectivity.
Applications are assessed for technical coexistence and competition impacts.

sources.title: Statement: Non-geostationary satellite systems – licensing updates
facts: Ofcom identifies NGSO systems as a means of expanding high-capacity connectivity and improving hard-to-reach broadband access.
The licensing approach seeks to enable multiple systems while managing interference and competition risks.
The page preserves consultation, statement and supporting guidance as separate evidence stages.

sources.title: Statement: Updating fees for Satellite Gateways
facts: Ofcom updated the fee framework for NGSO gateways and applied relevant elements to GSO gateways.
The decision replaces cost-based annual fees for NGSO gateways with administered incentive pricing.
Lower band factors were introduced for Q/V and E-band spectrum.

sources.title: Statement and further consultation: Expanding spectrum access for satellite gateways
facts: Ofcom opened up to 10 GHz of Q/V-band spectrum for satellite gateways in low-density areas.
The low-density authorisation area covers about 94% of UK landmass.
Additional access in high-density areas remained subject to further consultation.

sources.title: Statement: Starlink application for two non-geostationary gateway earth station licences
facts: Ofcom granted Starlink NGSO gateway licences for Harlow and Mulberry Wharf.
The gateways connect to Starlink's NGSO satellite system.
Ofcom stated the decision should improve capacity and resilience, not establish household-level service availability.

sources.title: Statement: Inmarsat Global and Space Norway joint NGSO network licence
facts: Ofcom granted a joint NGSO network licence for the GX10 system in Ka-band frequencies.
The authorisation covers user terminals and potential commercial, government, aeronautical and maritime services.
A licence decision is regulatory evidence rather than current premises orderability evidence.

sources.title: Statement: NSLComm application for non-geostationary earth station network licence
facts: Ofcom granted NSLComm an NGSO network licence for BeetleSat user terminals.
The decision enables satellite connectivity services in the UK.
The page distinguishes the application, consultation, responses and final statement.

sources.title: Satellite earth stations
facts: Satellite earth stations communicate with space stations from the Earth's surface.
They support telephony, data, backhaul, broadcast and two-way broadband services.
The guidance links licence types, fees and frequency allocations.

sources.title: Space and satellites
facts: The portal consolidates Ofcom satellite licensing, consultation and decision material.
It lists current NGSO applications and gateway-spectrum work.
A portal index is lineage evidence and not a standalone coverage measurement.

sources.title: C-LEO Programme
facts: The C-LEO programme provides up to £160 million over six years for satellite-communications technology.
It targets UK companies and researchers developing LEO-constellation capabilities.
The collection identifies the programme and routes users to current calls.

sources.title: About the C-LEO Programme
facts: C-LEO aims to strengthen UK capability in high-volume satellite constellations.
Priority technologies include onboard processing, active antennas, optical links, networking and user terminals.
Supported projects are expected to demonstrate technological or engineering advancement.

sources.title: UK Space Agency C-LEO Call 2: ARTES Only
facts: Call 2 sought UK National Delegate support through ESA's ARTES programme.
The first-stage application deadline was 13 April 2026.
The collection separates application forms, guidance and proposal annexes.

sources.title: Guide to applying for C-LEO Call 2: ARTES Only
facts: The guide describes ARTES, C-LEO objectives and a two-stage application process.
The indicative stage-two deadline was 12 June 2026.
Funding-call milestones are programme administration and not deployed-connectivity evidence.
